# Summary

As the number of elements to process increases, running time grows accordingly. To analyze this, we **parameterize running time as a function of input size**, allowing us to understand how performance scales. Additionally, when analyzing running time, we generally focus on **upper bounds** — guarantees that the program won't exceed a certain time — because this provides users with meaningful, practical assurances. Knowing a program takes *at most* a certain amount of time is far more useful than knowing it takes *at least* that long, since a lower bound offers no guarantee of when it will finish.
